description.text: Angelica Kauffman was born on 30 October 1741 in Chur, Switzerland, and was raised in a family that moved through the Alpine regions of Switzerland, Austria, and Italy.  Trained by her father, the Austrian muralist Joseph Johann Kauffmann, she became a child prodigy, mastering four languages—German, Italian, French, and English—by the age of twelve and already receiving commissions from bishops and nobles.

Kauffman’s career flourished in London and Rome, where she became one of only two female founding members of the Royal Academy of Art in 1768.  She distinguished herself as a history painter—a rare and prestigious genre for women at the time—while also producing celebrated portraits, landscapes, and decorative works that earned her acclaim across Europe.

curiosities.text: She was one of only two women—alongside Mary Moser—to be a founding member of the Royal Academy of Art in London in 1768.
By the age of twelve, Kauffman was already painting for bishops and nobles, demonstrating her early mastery of the craft.

In addition to her artistic talent, she was a gifted singer and had to choose between a career in opera and painting after a Catholic priest warned her that opera was a dangerous place filled with "seedy people."
